questions.q: The 46XY DSD page divides its causes into two columns headed by the appearance of the external genitalia. Which pair?
opts: Male external genitalia and ambiguous genitalia
Female external genitalia and male external genitalia
Female external genitalia and ambiguous genitalia
questions.exp: Page 165 opens with 'Female external genitalia :' and 'Ambiguous genitalia :'.

questions.q: Which disorder heads the 'female external genitalia' column?
questions.exp: AIS is the first entry and is marked (m/c).

questions.q: Fill up: In the 46XY tree, AIS is annotated as ____ (most common).
questions.exp: The entry reads '(AIS) : m/c'.

questions.q: How many causes are printed in the 'female external genitalia' column?
questions.exp: Complete AIS, Swyer's syndrome, 5-alpha reductase deficiency and LH receptor defect.

questions.q: The third cause printed in the female-external-genitalia column is:
questions.exp: The order is complete AIS, Swyer's syndrome, 5-alpha reductase deficiency, LH receptor defect.

questions.q: The fourth cause in the female-external-genitalia column is:
questions.exp: LH receptor defect is numbered 4.

questions.q: Match each female-external-genitalia cause with its printed rank - 1) Complete AIS 2) Swyer's syndrome 3) 5-alpha reductase deficiency 4) LH receptor defect ... A) 3 B) 1 C) 4 D) 2
questions.exp: Printed order: 1 complete AIS, 2 Swyer's, 3 5-alpha reductase deficiency, 4 LH receptor defect.

questions.q: Which two disorders head the 'ambiguous genitalia' column?
questions.exp: The ambiguous column opens with 1. Partial AIS, 2. Ovotestis, then CAH variants.

questions.q: Fill up: The ambiguous-genitalia column groups four enzyme defects under the heading congenital ____ hyperplasia.
questions.exp: The heading reads 'Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)'.

questions.q: Which four enzyme defects are grouped under CAH in the 46XY ambiguous-genitalia column?
opts: 21-alpha hydroxylase, 11-beta hydroxylase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR
3-beta HSD, P450 OR, 5-alpha reductase and aromatase
17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 oxidoreductase
questions.exp: The four listed sub-bullets are 17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR deficiency.

questions.q: True/False: 21-alpha hydroxylase deficiency appears in the 46XY ambiguous-genitalia list.
opts: True - it is listed under female external genitalia
questions.exp: It is absent; the CAH sub-list here has only 17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is filed under 'ambiguous genitalia' rather than 'female external genitalia'?
questions.exp: Ovotestis is the second entry of the ambiguous column; the other three are in the female-external-genitalia column.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY infant is born with completely female-looking external genitalia. Which column of the printed tree should be searched first?
questions.exp: Complete AIS, Swyer's, 5-alpha reductase deficiency and LH receptor defect sit in the female-external-genitalia column.

questions.q: Fill up: The page heading reads '46 XY DSD (Disorders of Sexual ____)'.
questions.exp: The printed title expands DSD as Disorders of Sexual Development.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Which single 46XY DSD is the stated exception to the rule that these children are considered female at birth?
questions.exp: 'Considered as female child at birth - Except: Ovotestis'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Fill up: The presenting complaint common to these patients is ____ amenorrhoea at puberty.
questions.exp: 'Complaints of: 1. 1° Amenorrhea at puberty'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: A female with primary amenorrhoea and a complaint of inguinal hernia should raise suspicion of which karyotype?
questions.exp: 'Female with 1° Amenorrhea + C/o Inguinal hernia: Suspect XY genotype'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Bilateral inguinal hernia in this context points to:
questions.exp: 'B/L Inguinal hernia → Undescended testis'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Where are the abdominal gonads detected?
questions.exp: 'Abdominal gonads: Palpable on physical examination'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Fill up: Undescended testis in 46XY DSD carries an increased risk of ____.
questions.exp: Printed: '↑ Risk of malignancy'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: The treatment recommended for the undescended testis is:
questions.exp: 'Rx: Gonadectomy'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: The most common tumour associated with an undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Printed: 'm/c tumor associated with undescended testis: Gonadoblastoma'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: The most common malignancy associated with an undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Printed: 'm/c malignancy associated with undescended testis: Dysgerminoma'.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Match the label with the lesion - 1) m/c tumour 2) m/c malignancy ... A) Dysgerminoma B) Gonadoblastoma
questions.exp: Gonadoblastoma is the commonest tumour; dysgerminoma the commonest malignancy.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Scenario: A 16-year-old girl with primary amenorrhoea is found to have bilateral inguinal swellings that are palpable testes. What is the definitive management of those gonads?
questions.exp: The printed Rx for the undescended testis in 46XY DSD is gonadectomy because of malignancy risk.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: True/False: The risk quoted for these abdominal gonads is benign degeneration, so removal is optional.
opts: True - removal is deferred to age 40
True - only if the tumour marker rises
questions.exp: There is an increased risk of malignancy and gonadectomy is the recommended treatment.

questions.unit: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue
questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed as a shared characteristic of 46XY DSD?
opts: Virilisation at birth in every case
questions.exp: Virilisation at birth is not universal; the page stresses they are considered female at birth (except ovotestis).

questions.q: Fill up: Complete AIS is described as an ____ linked recessive disorder.
questions.exp: The printed line is 'X linked recessive disorder'.

questions.q: In complete AIS, the SRY gene status is:
questions.exp: 'SRY gene: N'.

questions.q: Which four structures are all marked 'N' (normal) at the top of the complete AIS diagram?
opts: SRY gene, ovary, Leydig cells and granulosa cells
Testis, epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicle
SRY gene, testis, Mullerian duct and Wolffian duct
SRY gene, testis, Leydig cells and Sertoli cells
questions.exp: The diagram marks SRY gene N, testis N, Leydig cells N and Sertoli cells N.

questions.q: The testis in complete AIS produces testosterone that is:
opts: Normal in amount but the body is resistant to it
questions.exp: 'Testosterone: N but Resistant to testosterone'.

questions.q: Fill up: Sertoli cells are stimulated by ____, which is itself normal in AIS.
questions.exp: 'FSH (+)' drives Sertoli cells; 'FSH: N'.

questions.q: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which does what to FSH?
questions.exp: 'Inhibin B → -ve feedback on FSH'.

questions.q: The second Sertoli cell product named is Anti-Mullerian Hormone. Its action is:
questions.exp: 'Antimullerian hormone → Regression of mullerian duct'.

questions.q: Fill up: Because AMH acts normally, patients with complete AIS have no fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix or ____ vagina.
questions.exp: 'No fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, upper vagina'.

questions.q: Resistance to testosterone causes the Wolffian duct to:
opts: Fail to grow and then regress
questions.exp: 'Resistance to testosterone → Wolffian duct does not grow → Wolffian duct regresses'.

questions.q: Failure of scrotal descent in complete AIS leaves the testis:
questions.exp: 'Failure of scrotal descent → Abdominal testis'.

questions.q: Which two consequences are printed next to the abdominal testis?
opts: Increased chance of malignancy and bilateral inguinal hernia
questions.exp: Printed: '↑ Chance of malignancy' and 'B/L inguinal hernia'.

questions.q: Fill up: Testosterone is normally converted to DHT by ____ reductase; AIS patients are resistant to both.
questions.exp: The diagram shows 'Testosterone --5α reductase--> DHT' with 'Resistant to DHT'.

questions.q: Resistance to DHT produces:
opts: Failure of masculinisation of the external genitalia
questions.exp: 'Resistant to DHT → Failure of masculanisation of external genitalia'.

questions.q: The net genital outcome in complete AIS is:
opts: Female external genitalia, female at birth
questions.exp: The chain ends in 'Female external genitalia → Female at birth'.

questions.q: At puberty, testicular testosterone fails to produce secondary sexual development, giving pubic and axillary hair at Tanner stage:
questions.exp: 'Scanty pubic hair / axillary hair: Tanner stage 1 or 2' and 'Failure of 2° sexual development'.

questions.q: Why does breast development still occur in complete AIS?
opts: Estrogen is produced by the adrenal gland
Testosterone is aromatised to estrogen and estrogen is not resisted
questions.exp: The diagram shows 'Testosterone --Aromatase--> Estrogen (Not resistant)' leading to proper breast development.

questions.q: Breast development in complete AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.exp: 'Breast development (Proper): Tanner stage 4 or 5'.

questions.q: Fill up: AIS patients may have a ____ ending vagina.
questions.exp: 'may have blind ending vagina'.

questions.q: Match each AIS finding with its mechanism - 1) No uterus 2) No vas deferens 3) Female external genitalia 4) Breast development ... A) Estrogen not resisted B) AMH acted normally C) Wolffian duct regressed D) DHT resisted
questions.exp: AMH removes the uterus; testosterone resistance regresses the Wolffian duct; DHT resistance feminises the exterior; unopposed estrogen builds breast.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with well-developed breasts, scanty axillary hair, no menarche and a blind-ending vagina. Which internal anatomy is expected?
opts: No uterus, no fallopian tubes, no upper vagina
questions.exp: AMH works in AIS, so Mullerian structures are absent; the vagina is blind-ending.

questions.q: True/False: In complete AIS, the external genitalia are ambiguous.
questions.exp: Complete AIS gives female external genitalia; ambiguity belongs to partial AIS.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a consequence of androgen receptor resistance in complete AIS?
opts: Absent masculinisation of the external genitalia
questions.exp: Mullerian regression is driven by AMH, not by the androgen receptor.

questions.q: Fill up: GnRH is ____ in AIS because negative feedback is lost.
questions.exp: The hormonal profile block prints '↑ GnRH' with 'loss of negative feedback on GnRH'.

questions.q: Which gonadotrophin is raised and which is normal in AIS?
questions.exp: The inference line reads '↑ LH, (N) FSH'.

questions.q: Testosterone in AIS, compared with females, is:
questions.exp: 'Testosterone: ↑ (Compared to Females)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The Sertoli cell marker printed in the profile is inhibin ____.
questions.exp: Inhibin B is listed in the profile.

questions.q: The same 'raised LH with normal FSH' pattern is printed alongside which other diagnosis?
questions.exp: The inference compares AIS with PCOS.

questions.q: How does the menstrual presentation differ between AIS and PCOS in this comparison?
opts: AIS gives secondary amenorrhoea, PCOS primary
AIS gives primary amenorrhoea, PCOS gives secondary amenorrhoea
questions.exp: The two columns read '1° Amenorrhea' (AIS) and '2° Amenorrhea' (PCOS).

questions.q: Fill up: The comparison labels AIS with 1° amenorrhoea and PCOS with ____ amenorrhoea.
questions.exp: PCOS is printed under 2° amenorrhoea.

questions.q: Match the hormone to its printed direction in AIS - 1) GnRH 2) LH 3) FSH 4) Testosterone ... A) Normal B) Raised
questions.exp: GnRH, LH and testosterone are raised; FSH is normal.

questions.q: Scenario: A phenotypic woman with primary amenorrhoea has LH 18 IU/L, FSH 5 IU/L and testosterone in the male range. Which diagnosis does the printed inference support?
questions.exp: Raised LH, normal FSH and male-range testosterone with primary amenorrhoea is the AIS pattern.

questions.q: True/False: The AIS hormonal profile shows a suppressed GnRH from androgen excess.
opts: True - GnRH falls with androgen feedback
questions.exp: Androgen resistance removes feedback, so GnRH is raised.

questions.q: The first management instruction printed is to:
questions.exp: 'Continue identity of female'.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonadectomy of the intra-abdominal testis is timed after completion of breast development, at ____ years.
questions.exp: Printed: 'After breast development completion (14 to 16 yrs)'.

questions.q: Why is gonadectomy deferred rather than done in infancy in complete AIS?
opts: The testis is needed for growth spurts
The testis provides testosterone that is aromatised for breast development
Anaesthetic risk in infancy is prohibitive
The diagnosis cannot be made earlier
questions.exp: Pubertal oestrogen comes from aromatised testicular testosterone, so removal waits until breast development completes.

questions.q: Fill up: Estrogen replacement therapy is given, but ____ is not supplemented because the uterus is absent.
questions.exp: 'Progesterone: Not supplemented d/t absent uterus'.

questions.q: Vaginoplasty in AIS is timed:
questions.exp: 'Vaginoplasty - Just before/after marriage'.

questions.q: Which vaginoplasty technique is described as laparoscopic?
questions.exp: 'Vecchietti technique: Laparoscopic'.

questions.q: The first named vaginoplasty technique is:
questions.exp: '1. McIndoe vaginoplasty'.

questions.q: Can a woman with complete AIS have a biological child?
questions.exp: Printed note: 'Complete AIS cannot have biological child'.

questions.q: Match each management step with its timing - 1) Gonadectomy 2) Vaginoplasty 3) Estrogen replacement 4) Continue female identity ... A) Just before/after marriage B) Immediately C) After thelarche, 14-16 yrs D) After gonadectomy
questions.exp: Identity is continued from the outset; gonadectomy at 14-16 years; estrogen after it; vaginoplasty around marriage.

questions.q: Scenario: A 15-year-old with complete AIS has just completed breast development. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Gonadectomy is scheduled once breast development completes at 14-16 years.

questions.q: True/False: Progesterone is added to the estrogen regimen in complete AIS to mimic a normal cycle.
opts: True - it protects the vaginal remnant
questions.exp: Progesterone is not supplemented because there is no uterus.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT part of printed complete AIS management?
questions.exp: Testosterone is already high and resisted; it is never supplemented.

questions.q: Fill up: In partial AIS, males are ____ sensitive to androgens.
questions.exp: Printed: 'males are partially sensitive to androgens'.

questions.q: In partial AIS, testosterone acting through a partially functional receptor allows the Wolffian duct to:
questions.exp: 'Wolffian duct develops'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partial sensitivity to DHT gives ____ male internal genital organs.
questions.exp: 'DHT (Partial sensitivity) → Poorly formed of male internal genital organ'.

questions.q: The genital appearance at birth in partial AIS is:
questions.exp: 'Ambiguous genitalia'.

questions.q: How are partial AIS infants registered at birth?
questions.exp: 'Females at birth'.

questions.q: Why does partial AIS present with primary amenorrhoea?
questions.exp: '1° Amenorrhea d/t absent uterus'.

questions.q: Breast development in partial AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.exp: 'Breast: Tanner 4/5'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in partial AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.exp: 'Pubic & axillary hair: Tanner 1 or 2'.

questions.q: Which two local findings are printed together as features of partial AIS?
questions.exp: 'Clitoromegaly / Labioscrotal fusion'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partial AIS is the most common cause of ambiguous genitalia in ____ individuals.
questions.exp: Printed: 'm/c cause of ambiguous genitalia in 46 XY'.

questions.q: Partial AIS is also described as the most common cause of:
questions.exp: 'm/c cause of male pseudohermaphrodite'.

questions.q: How does the management of partial AIS differ from complete AIS regarding the gonads?
opts: Gonadectomy is done as soon as possible
The testes are left in place
questions.exp: 'Same as AIS. Gonadectomy as soon as possible'.

questions.q: Why is early gonadectomy advised in partial AIS?
opts: The testis is prone to torsion
The testis blocks the inguinal canal
questions.exp: The arrow reads 'Testis → Testosterone → Virilisation at puberty'.

questions.q: Match the partial AIS feature with its description - 1) Breast 2) Pubic hair 3) Internal genitalia 4) External genitalia ... A) Poorly formed male B) Ambiguous C) Tanner 4/5 D) Tanner 1 or 2
questions.exp: Breast Tanner 4/5, pubic hair Tanner 1-2, poorly formed male internal genitalia, ambiguous external genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A child reared female presents at 14 with clitoromegaly present since birth, Tanner 4 breasts, scanty pubic hair and no uterus. Which diagnosis fits?
questions.exp: Clitoromegaly present since birth with good breast development and absent uterus is the partial AIS picture.

questions.q: True/False: In partial AIS the internal genitalia are fully formed male structures.
questions.exp: They are described as poorly formed male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed feature of partial AIS?
questions.exp: Breasts develop to Tanner 4/5 in partial AIS.

questions.q: Fill up: Swyer syndrome has a ____ karyotype with dysgenetic testes.
questions.exp: The block prints '46 XY' with 'Gonads: Testis, Dysgenetic'.

questions.q: How many causes of the dysgenetic gonad are printed?
questions.exp: Causes: 1. Idiopathic, 2. Point mutation of SRY gene.

questions.q: Which gene is named in the second cause of Swyer syndrome?
questions.exp: 'Point mutation of SRY gene'.

questions.q: Fill up: The first listed cause of Swyer syndrome is ____.
questions.exp: '1. Idiopathic'.

questions.q: Both Leydig and Sertoli cells are described as:
questions.exp: Printed: 'Leydig cells (Dysgenetic)' and 'Sertoli cells (Dysgenetic)'.

questions.q: Absent testosterone in Swyer syndrome leads to failure of:
questions.exp: 'Absent testosterone → Failure of Wolffian duct development; male internal genitalia absent'.

questions.q: Absent AMH in Swyer syndrome results in:
opts: Mullerian duct formation and female internal genitalia
questions.exp: 'Absent AMH → Mullerian duct formation → Female internal genitalia'.

questions.q: Fill up: Absent inhibin B removes negative feedback on GnRH, so ____ rises.
questions.exp: 'Absent inhibin B → Absent -ve feedback on GnRH → ↑ FSH'.

questions.q: Absent DHT in Swyer syndrome gives:
questions.exp: 'Absent DHT → Female external genitalia'.

questions.q: How is a child with Swyer syndrome registered at birth?
questions.exp: 'Female child at birth'.

questions.q: Match the absent hormone with its consequence in Swyer syndrome - 1) Testosterone 2) AMH 3) DHT 4) Inhibin B ... A) Female external genitalia B) Female internal genitalia C) Male internal genitalia absent D) Raised FSH
questions.exp: No testosterone means no Wolffian derivatives; no AMH means Mullerian structures persist; no DHT means female exterior; no inhibin B means unopposed FSH.

questions.q: At puberty in Swyer syndrome, absent testosterone causes failure of female secondary sexual characteristics, specifically:
questions.exp: 'Failure of female 2° sexual characteristics formation: Absent breast'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in Swyer syndrome is:
questions.exp: 'Pubic hair & axillary hair: Scanty'.

questions.q: Which three presentations are printed for Swyer syndrome?
opts: Delayed puberty, primary amenorrhoea and bilateral inguinal hernia
Bilateral inguinal hernia, virilisation and acne
questions.exp: The presentation list is delayed puberty, 1° amenorrhoea and B/L inguinal hernia.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonadectomy in Swyer syndrome is advised ____ diagnosed, unlike in complete AIS.
questions.exp: 'Gonadectomy: As soon as diagnosed'.

questions.q: Estrogen supplementation is given for how long to achieve breast development?
questions.exp: 'Estrogen supplementation - For 1 year → Breast development'.

questions.q: Which additional procedure is listed after estrogen in Swyer management?
questions.exp: Vaginoplasty is the final listed step.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea, absent breast development, scanty pubic hair, a 46XY karyotype and bilateral inguinal gonads. Which diagnosis?
questions.exp: 46XY with absent breast development and dysgenetic gonads presenting as inguinal hernias is Swyer syndrome.

questions.q: True/False: In Swyer syndrome the uterus is absent because AMH is produced normally.
opts: True - AMH is only partly reduced
True - the uterus is hypoplastic instead
questions.exp: AMH is absent, so Mullerian structures including the uterus form.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding would argue AGAINST Swyer syndrome?
opts: Well-developed breasts at Tanner 5 without estrogen therapy
questions.exp: Swyer patients lack endogenous estrogen, so breasts do not develop without supplementation.

questions.q: Fill up: 5-alpha reductase deficiency occurs in a ____ individual with normally formed testes.
questions.exp: The block prints '46 XY' with 'Gonads: Testis (N)'.

questions.q: Which two testicular cell types are explicitly labelled normal in this condition?
questions.exp: 'Sertoli cells (N)' and 'Leydig cells (N)'.

questions.q: Testosterone acts normally on the Wolffian duct to produce:
questions.exp: 'Testosterone → Wolffian duct development → male internal genital organ'.

questions.q: AMH acts normally to:
questions.exp: 'AMH → Mullerian duct regress'.

questions.q: Fill up: The defect is the failure of conversion of testosterone to ____.
questions.exp: 'Defect: Testosterone --5α reductase--> DHT' is blocked.

questions.q: Because DHT is absent, the external genitalia at birth are:
questions.exp: 'Female external genital organs → Female at birth'.

questions.q: At puberty, normal testosterone produces which two male secondary sexual characteristics?
opts: Increased muscle mass and deepening of voice
questions.exp: 'male 2° sexual characteristics: ↑ muscle mass, Deepening of voice'.

questions.q: Fill up: Absence of DHT means pubic and axillary hair are ____.
questions.exp: 'Absent pubic or axillary hair: d/t absent DHT'.

questions.q: Breast development in 5-alpha reductase deficiency is:
questions.exp: 'Absent breast development'.

questions.q: Which virilising event occurs at puberty in this condition?
questions.exp: Under 'Virilisation': 'Clitoromegaly at puberty'.

questions.q: The printed note contrasts this condition with AIS by stating that in AIS:
questions.exp: 'Note: In AIS: Testosterone → Estrogen'.

questions.q: Why do AIS patients develop breasts while 5-alpha reductase deficient patients do not?
opts: In AIS, unopposed testosterone is aromatised to estrogen; in 5-alpha reductase deficiency testosterone drives virilisation instead
In AIS the ovaries are present
In 5-alpha reductase deficiency estrogen is destroyed
questions.exp: The note attributes AIS breast development to testosterone-to-estrogen conversion, which does not produce the same effect here where testosterone acts as an androgen.

questions.q: Match the timing of clitoromegaly - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Puberty B) Since birth
questions.exp: Partial AIS is since birth; 5-alpha reductase deficiency is at puberty.

questions.q: Match the breast finding - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Absent B) Tanner 4/5
questions.exp: Partial AIS has Tanner 4/5 breasts; 5-alpha reductase deficiency has none.

questions.q: Match the internal genitalia - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Fully formed male genitalia B) Poorly formed male genitalia
questions.exp: Partial AIS has poorly formed male internal genitalia; 5-alpha reductase deficiency has fully formed ones.

questions.q: How many rows does the printed partial AIS versus 5-alpha reductase deficiency comparison table have?
questions.exp: The rows are time of clitoromegaly, breast and internal genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A child reared female develops clitoromegaly, increased muscle mass and voice deepening at puberty, but has no pubic hair and no breasts. Karyotype 46XY. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pubertal virilisation with absent pubic hair and absent breasts in a 46XY patient is the 5-alpha reductase deficiency picture.

questions.q: True/False: In 5-alpha reductase deficiency the internal genitalia are poorly formed male structures.
questions.exp: Wolffian development proceeds normally, giving fully formed male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is a partial AIS feature rather than a 5-alpha reductase deficiency feature?
questions.exp: Since-birth clitoromegaly belongs to partial AIS; the other three belong to 5-alpha reductase deficiency.

questions.q: Which 46XY DSD is the only one in the tree that is shared with the 46XX chapter?
questions.exp: Ovotestis appeared in the 46XX chapter and reappears here under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: Fill up: The exception clause states that all 46XY DSD children are considered female at birth except ____.
questions.exp: The printed exception names ovotestis.

questions.q: Which investigation would confirm the suspected XY genotype in a female with primary amenorrhoea and inguinal hernia?
questions.exp: The chapter on ambiguous genitalia names karyotyping as the investigation of choice for suspected XY genotype.

questions.q: Fill up: Complete AIS is a receptor problem: the androgen ____ does not respond.
questions.exp: The heading 'Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome' with 'resistant to testosterone' localises the defect to the receptor.

questions.q: The page prints a heading 'Location:' immediately before 'COMPLETE AIS' and 'X linked recessive disorder'. What is the location implied by the mechanism?
questions.exp: The AIS block is a receptor-level defect; the location line precedes the genetics note.

questions.q: Which two hormones are produced normally by the Sertoli cells in complete AIS?
questions.exp: Sertoli cells give inhibin B and AMH; testosterone comes from Leydig cells.

questions.q: Fill up: LH in complete AIS is ____ because of loss of negative feedback.
questions.exp: The hormonal profile shows raised LH from lost androgen feedback.

questions.q: Why does FSH stay normal in complete AIS when LH rises?
opts: FSH is not under hypothalamic control
Inhibin B from Sertoli cells still feeds back on FSH
questions.exp: Intact Sertoli inhibin B keeps FSH in the normal range while androgen resistance raises LH.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY patient with complete AIS asks whether she can carry a pregnancy with IVF. What is the printed answer?
opts: Yes, with donor oocytes and surrogacy
No - she cannot have a biological child
Yes, with gestational carrier and her own oocytes
questions.exp: The printed note states complete AIS cannot have a biological child.

questions.q: Which vaginoplasty timing applies equally to complete AIS and Swyer syndrome?
questions.exp: Both pages time vaginoplasty around marriage.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Fill up: Swyer syndrome is also termed 46XY complete ____ dysgenesis.
questions.exp: The condition is a dysgenetic-gonad form of gonadal dysgenesis with a 46XY karyotype.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Which malignancy risk is printed for the intra-abdominal testis in complete AIS?
questions.exp: '↑ Chance of malignancy' is printed beside the abdominal testis.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Fill up: In Swyer syndrome, both LH and ____ are raised because of absent feedback.
questions.exp: Absent inhibin B and absent sex steroids raise both gonadotrophins.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Complete AIS management defers gonadectomy while Swyer management does it immediately. What is the reason for the difference?
opts: Swyer patients are older at diagnosis
In AIS the testis supplies aromatisable testosterone for breast development; in Swyer the gonad is dysgenetic and malignant
questions.exp: Functional AIS testes are kept until breast development completes; dysgenetic Swyer gonads are removed at diagnosis.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Which two vaginoplasty techniques are named across this chapter?
questions.exp: McIndoe vaginoplasty and the laparoscopic Vecchietti technique are the two named.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Fill up: In 5-alpha reductase deficiency, the external genitalia are female at birth but ____ at puberty.
questions.exp: Pubertal testosterone causes virilisation, notably clitoromegaly.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Which single feature separates 5-alpha reductase deficiency from complete AIS at puberty?
opts: Presence of virilisation and absent breasts
Presence of breasts and absent pubic hair
questions.exp: 5-alpha reductase deficiency virilises without breast development; complete AIS does the opposite.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: True/False: Both complete AIS and Swyer syndrome present with primary amenorrhoea and are reared female.
opts: False - Swyer patients are reared male
questions.exp: Both appear in the female-external-genitalia column and both present with primary amenorrhoea.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Match each 46XY DSD with its internal genitalia - 1) Complete AIS 2) Partial AIS 3) Swyer syndrome 4) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Female internal genitalia B) None C) Poorly formed male D) Fully formed male
questions.exp: AMH removes Mullerian structures in AIS and 5-ARD; absent AMH in Swyer leaves female organs; partial AIS gives poorly formed male organs.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Scenario: An infant with ambiguous genitalia is 46XY with palpable inguinal gonads. Which investigation choice makes the specific diagnosis rather than only the genetic sex?
opts: Karyotyping plus hormonal profiling of LH, FSH and testosterone
questions.exp: Karyotype establishes 46XY and the LH/FSH/testosterone pattern separates AIS from the enzyme defects in this chapter.

questions.unit: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons
questions.q: Odd one out - which 46XY DSD is NOT driven by a hormone-synthesis enzyme defect?
questions.exp: AIS is a receptor defect; the other three are CAH enzyme blocks.
